title: Israeli cabinet approves hostage release and four-day truce deal with Hamas
body:
In the early hours of Wednesday 22 November 2023, the Israeli cabinet approved a deal with Hamas for the release of hostages in exchange for a temporary pause in fighting. The vote was 35 in favour and three against, with only the three ministers from the Otzma Yehudit party, including National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, voting no, according to the Times of Israel.

Under the agreement, about 50 hostages, women and children, would be released in groups of 12 or 13 over four days. In return, Israel would release 150 Palestinian female and teenage security prisoners, chosen from a list of 300, none of whom had been convicted of murder. The pause in fighting, the first since the war began, could be extended by one day for every additional 10 hostages freed. Israel also agreed to allow more fuel and humanitarian aid into Gaza.

The deal was negotiated with Qatar as the lead mediator, working with the United States and Egypt. At the time, Israel said about 240 hostages were being held, while Al Jazeera cited 237 captives. Hamas said it held about 210 of them, with Palestinian Islamic Jihad believed to hold many of the rest. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the deal was difficult but right and that the war would not end until all hostages were freed and Hamas was defeated.
